content: The International Committee for Weights and Measures (CIPM), known in French as the Comité international des poids et mesures, is an organization composed of eighteen members from the Member States of the Metre Convention. Its primary responsibility is to ensure global uniformity in units of measurement. This is achieved either through direct actions or by submitting proposals to the General Conference on Weights and Measures (CGPM), also referred to in French as the Conférence générale des poids et mesures. It is important to note that the abbreviation ICWM is not used. A significant recent focus of the CIPM has been the establishment of the CIPM Mutual Recognition Arrangement (MRA), known in French as the Arrangement de reconnaissance mutuelle. This framework facilitates the mutual acceptance of measurement results conducted within the Member States of the Metre Convention. The CIPM convenes annually at the International Bureau of Weights and Measures (BIPM), or Bureau international des poids et mesures in French. During these meetings, the committee reviews reports submitted by its Consultative Committees. Additionally, the CIPM publishes an Annual Report detailing the administrative and financial status of the BIPM, which is distributed to the governments of the Member States of the Metre Convention.
